item.title: AFC North Roundup: Bengals cruise to division lead; Browns stay in playoff hunt
item.description: Even with three teams still firmly in playoff contention, the AFC North race officially has a new favorite, while another team’s playoff hopes are all but officially over. With Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Pittsburgh all multiple games over .500 entering Week 11, there’s a very real chance we’ll see all three teams in the 2026-27 NFL Playoffs. As for the Ravens, their latest defeat effectively eliminated them from postseason contention. Here’s a look at what took place in Week 10 for the AFC North. Bengals steamroll Steelers Cincinnati brought the fireworks. Pittsburgh supplied the audience. With first place in the AFC North at stake Sunday night, the Bengals overwhelmed the Steelers, 38-18, improving to 7-2 with their fifth consecutive victory. Pittsburgh slipped to 6-3 after spending much of the evening trying to keep a divisional showdown from becoming an even bigger embarrassment. The final margin hardly captures how thoroughly Cincinnati controlled the game, which stood at 24-3 by halftime and 31-3 entering the fourth quarter. Joe Burrow gave Pittsburgh almost no room to breathe. He completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, piling up 302 yards and three scoring passes before halftime. Against a defense that had been one of the best in the NFL over the past four weeks, Cincinnati’s quarterback repeatedly delivered. The Bengals have now scored at least 30 points in five consecutive games, establishing a franchise record and giving their winning streak some serious offensive muscle. Ja’Marr Chase was the problem Pittsburgh never solved. His 11 receptions produced 231 yards, including a 53-yard gain that helped set up Cincinnati’s second touchdown. Chase Brown caught touchdown passes of two and four yards, while Drew Sample and Dohnte Meyers also scored through the air. That distribution made the Bengals especially difficult to contain: Chase could rip apart the coverage between the end zones, and Burrow had several other answers when Cincinnati reached scoring territory. The defense made sure Burrow’s production came with a comfortable cushion. Cincinnati limited Pittsburgh to 222 total yards and 17 first downs while generating three sacks. Jonathan Allen, Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe each brought down Aaron Rodgers, whose passing line finished at 16 completions in 32 attempts for 145 yards. Pittsburgh managed only a field goal through three quarters, leaving its offense with far too much ground to cover when the touchdowns finally arrived. Rodgers connected with DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth for fourth-quarter touchdowns, but Cincinnati answered the first of those scores with a one-yard Samaje Perine touchdown run. The Bengals finished with a 484-222 advantage in total offense and held the ball for 35:09. Those numbers tell the story of a team that dictated the evening on both sides of the ball. item.title: Sixers comeback thwarts Magic, Heat stay hot
item.description: LeBron James celebrates as the Philadelphia 76ers clinch a comeback win over the Orlando Magic (Rich Storry) The Philadelphia 76ers produced another double-digit comeback to defeat the Orlando Magic 121-116 and extend their lead at the top of the NBA Eastern Conference on Wednesday. Joel Embiid led the Sixers' scoring with 26 points while V.J. Edgecombe produced a decisive 13-point fourth-quarter burst in a 24-point performance as Philadelphia improved to 13-3. LeBron James also weighed in with 22 points after the Sixers recovered from a 17-point first-quarter deficit to claw their way back and extend their winning streak to four games. It was the sixth time this season the Sixers have come back to win after trailing by 10 points or more. Philadelphia coach Nick Nurse admitted he had feared the worst after watching a rampant Orlando score 40 points in the first quarter. "They were just flying around at 100 miles an hour and we weren't right," Nurse said. "They were really putting it on us. We had to try to change a few things and change the rhythm of the game. "Sometimes that works and sometimes it doesn't." Philadelphia trailed until midway through the fourth quarter, taking the lead with just over five minutes remaining via a Jabari Walker three-pointer. "We did a very nice job tonight of our execution offensively down the stretch," Nurse said. "We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn't used before, and ran all that stuff very well and very calmly and with composure." The Miami Heat continued their march up the standings with a sixth straight win in a 137-130 defeat of the Milwaukee Bucks. Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 27 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists against his former club while Bam Adebayo added 26 points. Davion Mitchell rattled in six three-pointers in a 24-point gem. Miami, who improved to 9-6, were always in control in a wire-to-wire victory that saw them lead by as many as 30 points in the fourth quarter. The Bucks have now lost 11 straight and remain at the foot of the table. In Cleveland, the Memphis Grizzlies improved to 11-4 with a 124-121 defeat of the Cavaliers in a game that saw the lead change hands 22 times. Cam Spencer led Memphis with 26 points as Donovan Mitchell's 34-point display for Cleveland ended in defeat. rcw/pst

item.title: Lakers star Luka Doncic is having a month no other has had since 1960 Wilt Chamberlain
item.description: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Lakers star Luka Doncic is having a month no other has had since 1960 Wilt Chamberlain appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic is putting together a November for the history books with the Los Angeles Lakers , and the only name that can match it is Wilt Chamberlain . According to OptaSTATS , Doncic is averaging 40.4 points per game this month, and the Lakers have gone a perfect 8-0 in those games. The only other player in NBA history to average at least 40 points with an 8-0 team record through his first eight games of a month was Chamberlain in January 1960. Doncic’s latest outing came in Tuesday’s 118-114 overtime win over the Charlotte Hornets . He finished with 36 points, seven assists and six rebounds, and he set up Quentin Grimes for the game-tying 3-pointer at the end of regulation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The month has been full of eye-popping performances. Doncic poured in 40 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in a win over the Sacramento Kings on Nov. 4 . Two days later, he exploded for a season-high 53 points against the Portland Trail Blazers, which also made him just the fourth player in Lakers history to score 40 or more in four straight games , joining Kobe Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan. Doncic has led the league in scoring for much of the season and is on pace to become the first player since Chamberlain to average 40 points over a full campaign. His previous career-best average was 33.9 points per game with the Dallas Mavericks in 2023-24. JJ Redick has marveled at his star . “It feels like a supernova, but it also feels normal. We live on a spaceship, and we’re going at the speed of light at all times when he’s on the court,” he said. Doncic, however, has kept his focus on the bigger picture. “As long as we win the game, I’m fine,” he said earlier this month. The Lakers have done plenty of that. Los Angeles has won nine straight games and owns the NBA’s best record at 13-3. Doncic and the Lakers will look to keep the streak going when they host the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. item.title: Lando Norris jokes he "found the limit of a champagne bottle" in Brazil podium mishap
item.description: Motorsport photo 2025 Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has joked about how he "found the limit of a champagne bottle" for the first time in his career during his chaotic podium celebrations at the Brazilian Grand Prix. The McLaren driver won from pole at Interlagos, but his trademark celebration went wrong. As he slammed the champagne bottle down on the floor, it shattered in his hands. To make matters worse, he then walked into the podium sparks. While speaking to the media during the drivers' press conference ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Norris was asked whether he would be changing his post-race celebrations after the incident. "Yeah, that was the hardest part of the weekend," he said. "I guess you'll find out on Sunday if I'm on the top step. I mean, I never do that if I'm not first. So I need to try to win another race for you guys to find out. "But for the first time in my career, I found the limit of a champagne bottle. So I'm happy I finally managed to find it." Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren The Briton played down the effect of the sparks. "I did also walk into the sparks, which didn't help. But that was fine. I barely noticed it. I just kind of felt my ear was pretty hot, but it didn't burn me or anything," he said. "So yeah, not my finest couple of seconds, but also one for the memory books down the road. So I saved a little bit of the bottle. There's probably still some up on the podium in Brazil, but yeah, you'll find out when I next win." The incident came at the end of what Norris called "a mega weekend". He took pole position in the wet and went on to win the race, his third victory of the season. Norris admitted, however, that McLaren had not quite matched Mercedes for outright dry pace in Brazil, and that the tricky conditions had helped. With three races remaining in the 2026 season, Norris currently sits sixth in the drivers' standings. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Granby/Canton vs. CREC football game moved to Veterans Stadium in New Britain
item.description: Granby/Canton's football game against CREC on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, has been moved from Trinity College in Hartford to Veterans Stadium in New Britain. (Getty Images) Granby/Canton's football game against CREC on Friday night has been moved to Veterans Stadium in New Britain. The game will kick off at 6 p.m., Friday. The game was originally scheduled to be played at Trinity College in Hartford on Friday, with CREC as the host team, but CREC honored a request to move the game, according to CIAC executive director Glenn Lungarini. "The CIAC worked with CREC and Granby Memorial administration to move their game to Veterans Stadium in New Britain," Lungarini said. "CREC athletic administration was responsive and understanding of the request to move the game. The CIAC is providing CREC with financial and personnel support for that game." Granby/Canton is 7-2 and in fourth place in the Class S standings. The Bears can clinch a playoff berth with a win over CREC (0-8). Granby/Canton had its last game against the Hartford co-op at Weaver suspended after a fight broke out in the fourth quarter. The game was deemed completed the next day with Granby/Canton awarded the win 19-12, the score at the time of the suspension. Another fight occurred following the game and led to the arrests of two juveniles, one of whom had a loaded semi-automatic gun in a backpack . Police did not release the names of those arrested because they are juveniles. The Hartford co-op was scheduled to play Coginchaug/East Hampton/Classical at Coginchaug High School as part of the Week 11 schedule, but that game has been cancelled with the Coginchaug co-op awarded a forfeit win . item.title: ‘Get negative’ – Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro ignoring each other after their fight has fans hyped
item.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro had a falling out following the latter’s trade to the Milwaukee Bucks, which allegedly ended in a violent altercation. Adebayo and Herro allegedly got into it in Las Vegas during the NBA Summer League, with reports suggesting their relationship had deteriorated to such an extent after seven years as teammates. However, how the two acted around each other in their first game against each other has many fans hoping this could be the start of another NBA rivalry. Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro ignoring each other doesn’t shock NBA fans Ahead of the Miami Heat’s game against the Milwaukee Bucks, fans had their eyes glued to Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro, as this was set to be their first time engaging with each other in public since the incident in Las Vegas. Unsurprisingly, the two haven’t made amends just yet, as both stars ignored each other in the pre-game warm-up and proceeded to greet all the other players. Understandably, this moment had many NBA fans talking, as they felt that Bam and Herro were not going to be on the same page. One fan seemed to enjoy the hostility, simply remarking: “Let’s get negative.” Another fan likened their silence to a situation most people in life will have experienced: “Bam and Herro treated pregame like a group chat nobody’s replying to.” A third fan seemed to criticise both players for still harbouring a grudge: “NBA players are the softest people on earth.” A fourth fan suggested this interaction was a preview of how Adebayo was going to approach the game: “So Bam knew he was going to be on b******* from jump.” Hilariously, a fifth fan compared their feud to another high-profile NBA falling out: “Walmart Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.” And lastly, one Miami Heat fan lamented the state of their relationship: “Bam and Herro acting like strangers at the tip when they are supposed to run the pick-and-roll together.” At the time of this writing, Adebayo is out of the game as the Heat are on track to defeat the Bucks by a significant 20-point margin. Herro did not have a good game against his former team, scoring just eight points on 4/11 shooting, while going 0/5 from deep. On the other end, Adebayo led the Heat in scoring, putting up 26 points on 7/15 shooting from the field and 3/8 shooting from beyond the arc. If their rivalry proves to be a years-long chess game with both sides going back and forth, Adebayo has just made the first big move over Herro. item.title: FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on
item.description: Gianni Infantino has been leading Fifa since 2016 [Getty Images] The Football Association has considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, BBC Sport can reveal. But it believes any attempt to prevent him from standing in the election in March is likely to fail. The FA has also confirmed it is backing rival candidate Philippe Diallo. Infantino oversaw the introduction of a three-term limit when he replaced Sepp Blatter as leader of world football's governing body. However, Fifa's council agreed in 2022 that his first period in office from 2016 to 2019 should not count as it was the remainder of his predecessor's interrupted final term after resigning. Earlier this month, human rights campaign group Fair Square wrote to the FA claiming that the decision is open to legal challenge and was "contrary to the spirit and purpose" of Fifa statutes. It urged the FA to ask Fifa's governance committee to bar Infantino from the election in March because he has already served the maximum three terms. FA chair Debbie Hewitt has now replied, telling Fair Square that the governing body "has explored the possibility of challenging Mr Infantino's eligibility to run for a further term as the Fifa president but does not consider that such a challenge would secure the outcome sought". In correspondence seen by the BBC, Hewitt adds: "Ultimately the process followed Fifa's governance and led to an outcome where Mr Infantino's part term was disregarded for the purposes of maximum term limits. "Having considered the process in detail, we do not believe that a challenge would succeed." In a statement, Fair Square said: "It's understandable that the FA has no faith in Fifa's internal processes to hold Infantino accountable for serious breaches of the rules, but it's a mistake to abandon these channels, not least because it sends a signal to Infantino that he can do whatever he likes. "We will encourage the FA to leave its options open where this matter is concerned not least because Debbie Hewitt's position on the Fifa council puts her in a very strong position to demand clear answers on why Fifa discounted Infantino's first term." Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - has said a national association or confederation may need to challenge Infantino's eligibility at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas). However he has also said that the ability of European football associations to do so has been made harder by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin deciding to stand for a fourth term earlier this year. Ceferin reversed a previous insistence, in 2024, he would not seek re-election. The FA was among a number of national associations to withdraw its support of Infantino in the wake of the crisis sparked by his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors. item.title: Home ice not nice for Wings; fall 4-1 to Boston
item.description: DETROIT - Returning home after a long road trip didn't prove to be any sort of tonic for the Red Wings. The Wings took an early lead Wednesday, Nov. 18, but couldn't hold it, as Boston rolled to a 4-1 victory. J.J. Peterka and Pavel Zacha (power play) scored Boston goals in the second period, erasing a 1-0 Wings lead. David Pastrnak then provided some cushion in the period giving the Bruins a 3-1 lead. Casey Mittelstadt ended the scoring with his eighth goal, into an empty net, with 54.8 seconds remaining. The Wings (8-11-3, 19 points) lost their sixth game in the last seven, and seven of their last nine. Goaltender Daniil Tarasov stopped 26 shots for the Wings, keeping the game tight in the first period with several big saves. Boston's Jeremy Swayman made 19 saves. The Bruins (14-7-1, 29 points) ended a three-game losing streak. Lucas Raymond scored his ninth goal in the first period, giving the Wings an early lead. Keegan Kolesar got the puck ahead to Andrew Copp, who with a Bruins' defenseman pinching, went on a 2-on-1 rush with Raymond. Copp fed Raymond for a one-timer that sailed past Swayman at 16:58. But the Bruins rallied in the middle period. Peterka tied it with his sixth goal. Mason Lohrei found Peterka skating down wing, and Peterka blistered a shot that snuck just under the crossbar and over Tarasov, at 2:49. After the Bruins killed a Wings' power play, a Moritz Seider tripping penalty put the Bruins on the power play. Zacha scored his sixth goal, at 11:48, after Pastrnak threw the puck at net and it bounced off a pad straight to Zacha in the slot. Pastrnak made it 3-1 in the third period with his 10th goal. Lohrei skated into the zone and found Pastrnak, who skated into the slot and blasted a shot past Tarasov at 5:11. tkulfan@detroitnews.com @tkulfan This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Home ice not nice for Wings; fall 4-1 to Boston

item.title: Jazz Head Coach Discusses The ‘Psychological Battle’ Of Stopping Luka Doncic And Facing Walker Kessler
item.description: Credits: Imagn Images The Utah Jazz will face the Los Angeles Lakers tonight in their second fixture of the season. The last time these two sides met, Luka Doncic dropped 52 points and fell just two rebounds short of a triple-double in a 132-123 Lakers win . Before the game, the Jazz head coach, Will Hardy , told the media about how the team prepared to stop Luka Doncic from going off tonight. Subsequently, he also shared his feelings about facing former Jazz player Walker Kessler . “I have written on my [white] board, ‘Hope is not a strategy.’ So that’s out,” Hardy said initially about how the Jazz prepared to defend Luka Doncic tonight. “It’s hard because you go back and watch the film afterward, and it tests your ability to be critical of yourself. And also to recognize that in certain moments, we did a really good job, and he was just better.” “It’s a psychological battle more than anything. Especially when he hits a couple of tough deep threes or throws a pass that maybe no one expected,” he further added . Luka Doncic had 52 points, 10 assists, and eight rebounds in their last meeting with the Jazz, shooting 17-30 from the field (56.7% FG) and 8-18 from beyond the arc (44.4% 3P). The former Jazz player, Walker Kessler, had little impact in the first game (finishing with just two points and seven rebounds) but has since settled into his role with the Lakers. Will Hardy also shared his thoughts on facing him on the court tonight and whether he regrets not finding a place for him to stay with the Jazz. “I value my relationship with him and all the experiences we went through together…. There was a long-standing relationship there. Ultimately, I’m happy for Walker as a human being because we have a real relationship. He’s a wonderful guy,” said Hardy on his relationship with Walker Kessler. “As far as thinking about him being with us, those are sort of dangerous places to get into because you start going down an unproductive road. This is our group we are focused on helping. I always want the guys that we have relationships with to do well; tonight we’re competing against him.” “But the nature of our business has always been that way. It’s something that we all adjust to. I saw Walker before the game, and it takes a second to recognize him in the Lakers’ gear, but we’re in it to compete tonight,” Hardy concluded . Ultimately, Hardy knows containing Doncic will require more than simply executing a defensive game plan, especially after witnessing his brilliance firsthand. Meanwhile, facing a former player like Walker Kessler adds another layer to the matchup. But the Jazz coach appears determined to set emotions aside and focus on getting his team a win tonight amid their struggles this season. It remains to be seen if the Jazz (2-13) can end the Lakers’ (13-2) nine-game winning streak tonight. All eyes will be on Luka Doncic and Walker Kessler’s performance and how the Jazz can counter this two-man threat tonight in Austin Reaves’ absence.

item.title: Lando Norris on "GTA VI": "I wasn't allowed to play it when I was younger"
item.description: Motorsport photo Lando Norris admits he won't be playing Grand Theft Auto VI during Formula 1's final triple-header of the season while also revealing that he wasn't allowed to play the popular franchise when he was a child. Rockstar Games' long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on Thursday, after more than a decade of waiting since the last game, Grand Theft Auto V, came to market in 2013. Norris, known for streaming and being a prominent gamer between race weekends, has said the now legendary series wasn't part of his life growing up. "No, I don't think so," he said on being asked if he'll be checking out the game between the last few races of the season. "I never really ever played GTA V , maybe a few times. I mean, it's a cool game and I enjoy it. I watch other people playing and stuff like that. But yeah, not my cup of tea," Norris said in the drivers' press conference ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The McLaren driver explained that his parents had kept him from playing the game when he was growing up, likely due to its high age rating. "I would love to, but I wasn't allowed to play it when I was younger. I wasn't allowed. So when we would go on a school trip and I could nick someone else's PSP or something, it was the best trip of my life because I could finally get to play it," he said. "But I never grew up playing it when I was at home. I never really played it when I was older, therefore. So it's never been my thing. But I know a lot of people around the world are playing it right now. So maybe my mind changes. But for now, it's a no." Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren Not every driver shares his view. Aston Martin's Lance Stroll said he would "probably fire it up at some point for sure", while Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas said he had other plans. "Not my plan. I think there's better things to do out there. You know, the outside world is quite beautiful. It's quite nice going outside," Bottas said. Norris will have little time for gaming over the coming weeks anyway. F1's final triple-header takes him from Las Vegas this weekend to Qatar and then Abu Dhabi. The 27-year-old has plenty to race for. McLaren is 17 points behind Red Bull in the fight for third in the constructors' championship, and Norris arrives in Las Vegas off the back of victory in Sao Paulo. He is sixth in the drivers' standings, 16 points off third place, in a five-way fight for runner-up behind world champion Kimi Antonelli. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images Outspoken radio host Dan Dakich says Clemson’s championship window has closed, but Swinney isn’t backing away from his belief that another national title is coming. Dabo Swinney built Clemson into one of college football’s premier programs. Now, after several seasons of disappointing results, some observers are beginning to wonder whether those championship days are gone for good. Dan Dakich has made up his mind. On the latest episode of his show, Don’t @ Me , the OutKick host delivered a blunt assessment of Swinney’s future at Clemson. Dakich acknowledged that the Tigers could still win an ACC championship, but he sees no realistic path to another national title under their longtime coach. “He may win a conference,” Dakich said. “But there is absolutely no shot he wins a national championship, and we can clip this.” Dakich went even further, saying he does not believe Swinney will win another championship during the remainder of his own broadcasting career. Clemson’s Recent Results Have Raised Serious Questions The criticism comes after another frustrating performance from the Tigers. Clemson fell 20-6 to Georgia Tech at home on Nov. 14, dropping to 6-4 overall and 4-3 in ACC play. The Tigers managed just 228 yards of total offense and failed to score an offensive touchdown for the second consecutive game. The loss was particularly damaging because Georgia Tech entered the matchup with just two wins in ACC play. Clemson had an opportunity to build momentum late in the season but instead delivered one of its most disappointing performances of the year. The bigger concern is that the problems extend beyond one game. Clemson is 13-10 over its last 23 games, including the current season, and its offense has struggled to find consistency. During a Wednesday night showdown rich with storylines, Adebayo at one point scored nine in a row and connected on a trio of 3-pointers over the opening two quarters. Of course, all the while, Giannis Antetokounmpo was facing the team he was synonymous with for 13 seasons. And the matchup was taking place in Miami’s Kaseya Center, which doubled as “Vice City” on the eve of the highly anticipated nationwide release of Grand Theft Auto VI . Antetokounmpo played the facilitator role with nine assists and still managed 27 points in the Heat’s 137-130 victory over the Bucks. Adebayo finished with 26 points.
